definitions.gloss: the Nihon Shoki; the Chronicles of Japan
definitions.explanation: Japan's first official history, finished in 720 under Prince Toneri. Written in classical Chinese, it runs from the age of the gods to the reign of Empress Jitō.

examples.japanese: {日本書紀|にほんしょき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
{日本書紀|にほんしょき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧720⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{完成|かんせい}した→完成する：25528_kanseisuru⟧。
examples.english: The Nihon Shoki was completed in 720.

examples.japanese: {日本書紀|にほんしょき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}かれ→書く：00477_kaku⟧、⟦{古事記|こじき}→古事記：31027_kojiki⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{詳|くわ}しく→詳しい：02483_kuwashii⟧⟦{歴代|れきだい}→歴代：13199_rekidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{天皇|てんのう}→天皇：04546_tennou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{事績|じせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{記|しる}している→記す：14238_shirusu⟧。
examples.english: The Nihon Shoki is written in classical Chinese and records the deeds of successive emperors in more detail than the Kojiki.

notes:
SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{古事記|こじき}→古事記：31027_kojiki⟧: finished eight years earlier (712); a continuous story told in a Japanized style, while the {日本書紀|にほんしょき} is a year-by-year chronicle in classical Chinese, the first of the six official histories ({六国史|りっこくし})

USAGE:
- The two are often named together as {記紀|きき}, as in {記紀|きき}⟦{神話|しんわ}→神話：00367_shinwa⟧ (the myths of the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki)
